newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna airport shares dive 14 pct on results. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Vienna airport shares dive 14 pct on results. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Vienna airport operator Flughafen Wien AG on Thursday rattled investors with a limp set of first half earnings and a warning it did not expect its full year earnings to match 1995's.

The share price dived 14 percent to a new low for the year at 615 schillings in heavy trade after Flughafen said first-half pre-tax profit fell 4.4 percent to 389 million schillings ($36.56 million). Net profit dropped 5.4 percent to 263 million.
"It's a disaster. The results are very, very disappointing -- the market consensus was way above the actual results," said Alfred Reisenberger, analyst at IMI Sigeco in London.

Reisenberger said he had pre-tax profit pegged at 470 million schillings and net profit at 330 million. He now plans to revise down his forecast for earnings per share for the full year to 33 or 34 schillings from 39.
Creditanstalt analyst Isolde Kuehhas said she would revise down EPS to 28-30 schillings from a former forecast of 35.

Analysts said the main surprise in the first-half earnings was a 75 million schillings provision for marketing costs, linked to efforts to lure more long-haul traffic to Vienna. They added the company was expected to make a similar provision for the second half.

"Austrians are particularly cautious -- the management's being conservative. But from the shareholder point of view it's a bit silly and they're furious, as you can see from the share price," one analyst said.
Analysts said that while the first half was disappointing, the second half was traditionally the stronger due to seasonal factors.

Austria this year suffered one of its coldest and longest winters in decades, causing Flughafen to suffer huge operating expenses of 1.64 billion schillings (Corrects figure), up 12 percent or 177 million schillings, on the year-ago period, of which 95 million was purely for de-icing.
"It's very unlikely you're going to have two consecutive years of such severe temperatures," Reisenberger said.
The analysts pointed out that after closer scrutiny of the first half earnings, it was evident the underlying performance of Flughafen showed strong potential for future growth.
Total turnover climbed seven percent to 1.915 billion schillings, while passenger traffic increased 8.1 percent to 4,256,348 passengers. Flughafen said it expected a further increase in traffic.
Take-offs and landings increased 10.9 percent to 76,055, maximum take-off weight jumped 13.7 percent and long-haul flights surged 21.7 percent to 150,000 passenger departures. ($1=10.64 Schilling)
